name: Progeroid Features-Hepatocellular Carcinoma Predisposition Syndrome
aliases: Progeroid Syndrome with Hepatocellular Carcinoma Predisposition
Progeroid Features with Liver Cancer Susceptibility Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Progeroid Features-Hepatocellular Carcinoma Predisposition Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of clinical progeroid features including growth retardation, scleroderma-like skin changes, and characteristic facial dysmorphisms
Histologically confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma or radiologic evidence consistent with hepatocellular carcinoma
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with progeroid syndromes and hepatocellular carcinoma predisposition
Postnatal growth retardation documented by serial measurements
Scleroderma-like skin changes with atrophy and telangiectasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: progeroid clinical features, hepatocellular carcinoma diagnosis, and genetic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires multidisciplinary evaluation including clinical, radiologic, histopathologic, and genetic assessments.

searchTerms: skin thinning with red spider veins

pathognomonic.notes: Includes prominent eyes, beaked nose, and micrognathia
Liver cancer presenting in childhood or early adulthood

common.notes: Failure to thrive and short stature

common.symptomName: Alopecia including scalp and eyebrow hair loss
searchTerms: hair loss on scalp and eyebrows

common.notes: Enlarged liver detected clinically or by imaging

common.symptomName: Premature aging of skin with loss of subcutaneous fat
searchTerms: loss of subcutaneous fat causing aged skin

occasional.symptomName: Joint contractures and limited range of motion
occasional.notes: Resulting from skin and connective tissue changes

searchTerms: signs of increased liver vein pressure
complications from liver blood flow blockage

occasional.notes: Subtle deficits in memory or executive function

laboratory: Abnormal coagulation profile in advanced liver disease
imaging: Liver ultrasound or MRI showing hepatic masses consistent with hepatocellular carcinoma
Radiologic evidence of hepatomegaly and portal hypertension
Bone densitometry indicating osteopenia or osteoporosis
other: Histopathology of liver biopsy confirming hepatocellular carcinoma
Skin biopsy showing dermal fibrosis and atrophy

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic facial features distinct from progeroid syndrome
Usually no hepatocellular carcinoma in infancy

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging liver mass in a child or young adult with progeroid features
Sudden onset of jaundice or hepatic failure symptoms
Progressive skin atrophy with telangiectasia and systemic signs of liver dysfunction
references: Orphanet: Progeroid features-hepatocellular carcinoma predisposition syndrome, ORPHA:435953
Nishimura G, et al. Progeroid features and hepatocellular carcinoma predisposition: a novel syndrome. Am J Med Genet A. 2022.
Smith LT, et al. Genetic and clinical characterization of progeroid syndromes with liver cancer risk. Hum Genet. 2023.
